The system · Fully automated

How the business sells — without a single phone call

Every step that agencies normally do on calls happens here in writing, on a system. The client gets speed and proof; MAS gets a pipeline that runs while the team delivers. If a step works for the client, it stays automated — that's the test for every part below.

Step 1 · Attract

One link, everywhere

LinkedIn posts, Upwork proposals, referrals and the MAS network all point to one thing: the probe menu on this page. No “book a call” button anywhere — the offer is a task, not a meeting.

Automated: every outreach message ends with the same probe link and a pre-filled WhatsApp opener.

Step 2 · Order

Probe ordered by message

The client taps WhatsApp or email, the probe and price are already in the message, and payment is a single invoice link (Payoneer). No negotiation thread, no proposal deck.

Automated: pre-filled order messages per probe; invoice sent on first reply.

Step 3 · Intake

A form, not an interview

A short intake form collects everything delivery needs: business details, links, brand assets, and view-only account access with step-by-step screenshots. Questions after that are single messages, answered in the thread.

Automated: one form per probe; access instructions written once, reused forever.

Step 4 · Deliver

Proof lands in 48–72 hours

The probe arrives in the same thread it was ordered in, written to explain itself: findings, the work, and what to do next. This delivery — not a pitch — is what sells the retainer.

Automated: delivery templates per probe, so quality and format never depend on who's on shift.

Step 5 · Convert

The follow-up sequence asks for the big one

After delivery, a timed message sequence recaps the result, credits the probe fee, and offers the matching retainer with a package already built. Silence gets polite, spaced nudges — never a cold call.

Automated: Day 0 / 2 / 5 / 9 sequence below; stops the moment the client replies.

Step 6 · Retain

The retainer runs async too

Daily 08:00 Brain briefs, drafts to approve by replying YES, monthly ROI report in writing. Renewal is the default — the client cancels by message, so the work has to keep earning its place.

Automated: briefs, approval prompts, reports and invoices all run on schedule.

The conversion sequence — probe delivered, then the retainer ask

Four short messages, sent only until the client replies. Each one leads with what the probe found, not with MAS.

Day 0 · With delivery“Here's your probe. The headline: [top finding]. If we ran this monthly, [specific gain]. Your $ fee is credited if you start within 14 days.”
Day 2 · The proof recapOne screenshot or number from the probe + the exact retainer package it maps to, price included. One tap to say yes.
Day 5 · The cost of waiting“The leak in Fix #1 is costing roughly [amount] a month. The retainer pays for itself if we close half of it.”
Day 9 · The clean close“Your probe credit expires in 5 days. Want me to hold it, or shall I close the file?” A clear no is a fine answer — the door stays open.

Execution

The 90-day plan — automate first, then sell probes

Build the no-call machine first, then feed it prospects. Sequenced so probe revenue arrives in week one and retainer revenue funds the deeper AI layer.

Days1–30 · Automate & probe

Set up the machine, sell the first probes

Everything a prospect touches gets built once and reused: this page with the probe menu, pre-filled WhatsApp / email order messages, one intake form per probe, Payoneer invoice links, and delivery templates. Then work the US network MAS already has — 52+ US contacts from consultancy and dispatch work, plus LinkedIn and Upwork — with one message: “don't book a call, try a $99 task.”

  • Probe system live: order messages, intake forms, invoice links, delivery templates for all 4 probes
  • Follow-up sequence loaded (Day 0 / 2 / 5 / 9) so every delivered probe gets the retainer ask automatically
  • Outreach list: 50 US prospects (home services, dental / med spa, law firms, e-commerce, local multi-location) — LinkedIn + email + WhatsApp, all pointing at the probe menu
  • Upwork proposals reframed as probes: fixed-price audit / content tasks that end with a retainer offer
Exit goal: 8–12 probes sold and delivered; first 2 retainers converted from probes
Days31–60 · Convert & deliver

Turn probes into retainers, run them async

Probe volume is the pipeline now: every delivery is a case for the retainer, and the sequence does the asking. Signed clients are onboarded by form, connected (Meta, Google, GA4, CRM, reviews) with their permission, and run entirely in threads — calendars, content, ads, approvals by reply. The “Brain” in month two is Leo + a spreadsheet, and that's fine: clients buy the brief and the ROI clarity, not the plumbing.

  • Track probe → retainer conversion; the probe that converts best becomes the headline offer
  • Manual 08:00 brief (client's US time zone) for retainer clients, from their real numbers — cost per lead front and centre
  • Before/after results from probes and retainers documented as written case studies — they become the next round of outreach proof
  • Ask every happy probe client, by message, for 2 introductions — referrals feed the same probe link
Exit goal: 3–4 retainers running with zero calls held + 1 case study published
Days61–90 · Automate

Build Brain MVP v1 — deepen the automation

Automate what month two did by hand — the same pattern as your TenderBD scraper and DSE feed: scheduled pulls, one database, a small API, a brief generator on top. Sales automation and delivery automation become one system.

  • Meta Ads + Google Ads + GA4 scheduled data pulls for retainer clients
  • Brief generator: changes vs. baseline → ranked actions → Slack / email / WhatsApp at 08:00 US time
  • Content Generator wired to each client's brand voice and past top posts
  • Probe delivery partially automated too: the Brain Brief Probe is generated from the same pipeline, so a $99 order takes minutes of human time
  • Brain becomes a named line on every invoice — Launch add-on, included in Growth+
Exit goal: Brain live for retainer clients; probe delivery time cut in half
AfterDay 90 · Productise

Turn the edge into the product

With paying US proof, decide the bigger bets: sell the Brain white-label to other small US agencies, launch the founder bootcamp (Trifid's flywheel), or raise Hybrid Partner for US mid-market clients — all still sold probe-first, in writing.

  • Bootcamp cohort 1: teach the MAS content system, 7 days, paid, run over messages and recorded lessons
  • Brain pricing tested standalone for non-retainer US clients
  • Hire against demand only — editor first, then a second strategist
Rule throughout: no enterprise rebuild, and no step that only works on a call. If it can't be sold, delivered and renewed in writing, it doesn't ship.
The automation stack

How the no-call machine is built

Nothing here needs new infrastructure to start. It reuses the stack already running the MAS site and data products — now pointed at selling and serving US clients without calls.

Delivery base: 73, Eastern Commercial Complex, Kakrail, Dhaka — working US hours. Overnight production in Dhaka means content, reports and the Brain brief are ready before the US workday starts.

Selling layer — this page + messagesProbe menu with pre-filled WhatsApp / email orders, package builder that sends itself, and one intake form per probe. No booking tool, no CRM theatre — the thread is the CRM.
Money layer — one link per orderPayoneer invoice / payment link sent in the thread for probes and retainers; probe fee auto-credited when a retainer starts within 14 days. Ad spend always stays in the client's own accounts.
Follow-up layer — the sequence runs itselfDay 0 / 2 / 5 / 9 conversion messages after every probe, plus the standing rule from MAS WhatsApp work: any client query unanswered for 24 hours gets a reminder, and follow-ups continue until it's answered or closed.
Brain data layer — the TenderBD patternScheduled Python pulls (Meta Ads API, Google Ads, GA4) into PostgreSQL/SQLite with a FastAPI read API — the same shape as the tender scraper and DSE feed.
Brief & content engines — where Leo does the thinkingNumbers in, ranked plain-language actions out at 08:00 US time; hooks, captions and ad angles drafted from each client's own top performers, then finished by humans. Every action waits for a YES reply.
What Leo won't build (yet)24/7 real-time monitoring, self-serve signup, multi-agency SaaS — and anything that needs a phone call to sell. It comes after clients pay for v1.
